proof_nl:
Fix an arbitrary positive integer d. Define
A := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}
and
B := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}.

We split the index set {1,...,b} into the disjoint union {1,...,a} union {a+1,...,b}. (If a=0 or a=b, one of these sets is empty, and the same argument still applies.) Therefore A is the disjoint union of A ∩ {1,...,a} and A ∩ {a+1,...,b}, and similarly for B.

For i with 1 <= i <= a, the definition gives e_i = i. Hence
|A ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.

For i with a < i <= b, the definition gives e_i = r+i. The map i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto the set {m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b}. Under this bijection, the condition d divides e_i is exactly the condition d divides m. Thus
|A ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b and d divides m}| = M_d(r+a,r+b).

Since the two pieces are disjoint,
|A| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(r+a,r+b).

Now do the same for B. Clearly,
|B ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.
Also, the identity map is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto {m in Z : a < m <= b}, so
|B ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : a < m <= b and d divides m}| = M_d(a,b).
Therefore,
|B| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(a,b).

By the hypothesis of the lemma, for this positive integer d we have
M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b).
Comparing the formulas for |A| and |B|, we obtain
|A| >= |B|,
that is,
|{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.

Because d was arbitrary, this holds for every positive integer d, exactly as claimed.

domain_restrictions: a, b, r are integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
The family e_i is only defined for indices i from 1 through b.
For i from 1 through b, e_i equals i when i <= a and equals r + i when a < i <= b.
d must be a positive integer whenever M_d is used or divisibility by d is discussed.
M_d(u, v) counts integers m with u < m <= v and d dividing m, where u and v are integers.
The counts in the conclusion are taken over the finite index set from 1 through b.
If b = 0, the index set from 1 through b is empty, so the counted sets are empty.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if every positive integer d has at least as many multiples in the interval from r + a to r + b as in the interval from a to b, then for every positive integer d the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides i.
quantifier_order: Fix integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
For each integer i with 1 <= i <= b, define e_i by a piecewise rule: e_i = i if i <= a, and e_i = r + i if a < i <= b.
For each positive integer d and integers u, v, define M_d(u, v) as the number of integers m satisfying u < m <= v and d divides m.
Assume that for every positive integer d, M_d(r + a, r + b) is at least M_d(a, b).
Conclude that for every positive integer d, the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing i.

statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. For 1 <= i <= b define an integer e_i by e_i = i when i <= a, and e_i = r+i when a < i <= b. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. If M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d, then for every positive integer d one has |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.

status_snapshot.last_transition_reason: The proof is a complete direct counting argument. For fixed positive d, it partitions the index set {1,...,b} into {1,...,a} and {a+1,...,b}, uses the definition e_i=i on the first part and e_i=r+i on the second, and identifies the second-part count with M_d(r+a,r+b). Doing the same for divisibility of i identifies the comparison count with M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality then gives the desired result. The proof matches the lemma statement and assembly role, and it uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
